newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols jump on futures slide.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols jump on futures slide.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond implied volatilities firmed Tuesday as the underlying futures crumbled following news of a surge in U.S. consumer confidence.

Options traders said a large purchase of at-the-money Treasury bond puts boosted volatility in July. A U.S. brokerage house bought 2,000 of the July 109-00 puts, paying premiums of 1-20/64 up to 1-23/64.
Late in the session, July volatility was quoted at 8.40 percent, up from 8.15 percent at the opening and up sharply from Friday's 7.65 percent.
Implied volatility for September bond options also rose slightly, climbing to 8.50 percent from 8.45 percent on the opening and 8.30 percent Friday.
In September options, a second trading house paid 39/64 to purchase 1,000 of the 112-00 calls covered against June bond futures at 108-26.
An early swift drop in the underlying futures sent bond volatilities on their upward path, traders said.
The Conference Board this morning said its May consumer confidence index soared to a 28-year high of 127.1, far outstripping market expectations.
Another sizable transaction involved the sale of 2,500 puts in far-out-of-the-money 105-00 July options.
In the afternoon, activity in options largely dried up, floor traders said.
June bond futures ended 15/32 lower at 108-23, off the session lows after testing key support at 108-17.

Eurodollar volatilities were mostly steady to higher, with September unchanged at 8.8 percent late in the session and December up 0.2 point at 10.9 percent. In the mid-curves, short-dated June volatility was steady at 13.0 percent while July slipped to 15.0 percent.
